body.p: In response to the Office Action dated June 16, 2023, please enter the following amendments and remarks in the above-identified patent application.
Claims 1-42 were present in the application. Claims 1, 20, 41, and 42 are independent claims, while claims 2-19 and 21-40 are dependent claims.

In this paper, claims 1, 5, 6, 9, 13, 15, 16, 17, 20, 21, 24, 25, 28, 35, 36, 41, and 42 are amended, and claim 39 is canceled without prejudice, waiver, or surrender of the subject matter contained therein.
Claims 1-38 and 40-42 are presently in the application. Re-examination and re- consideration of the remaining claims are respectfully requested.
Support for the remarks presented herein can be found in the specification as originally filed at least in paragraphs [0055] - [0063] and FIGS. 5 and 6. No new matter has been added.
Applicant respectfully traverses all rejections of all pending claims and earnestly solicits allowance of the newly presented claims.
Claim Interpretation
The Office considers the language of claims 13 and 20 as allegedly requiring interpretation under 35 U.S.C. § 112(f).

Applicant respectfully traverses the interpretation of the claim language as previously presented. However, in order to expedite prosecution, Applicant has amended claim 13 and claim 20 to recite that the action or function is performed by a "processor," which is a specific hardware device that does not invoke 35 U.S.C. § 112(f) interpretation. Thus, claims 13 and 20, and dependent claims 21-38 and 40, should not be interpreted under 35 U.S.C. § 112(f).
Claim Objections
Claims 1, 9, 16-17, 20, 28, 35-36, and 41-42 are objected to for various informalities.

Applicant thanks the Examiner for the thorough review of the claims and has clarified the claims in accordance with the Examiner's suggestions. Applicant respectfully requests that the objections be withdrawn.

Claims 5, 15, and 39 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as allegedly being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor regards as the invention.

Claim 39 has been canceled without prejudice, waiver, or surrender of the features contained therein, and claims 5 and 15 have been clarified to render the rejections moot. Applicant respectfully requests that the rejections be withdrawn.

Claims 1-42 stand rejected on the grounds of non-statutory double patenting as being unpatentable over claims 1-35 of U.S. Patent No. 11,449,021 in view of U.S. Publication No. 2015/0336271 (hereinafter "Spicer").

Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections. Further Applicant respectfully asserts that the claims as amended are patentably distinct from Spicer. Applicant further notes that according to the Office Action Spicer requires modification based on Warashina and therefore the claims must be patentably distinct from Spicer.
Claim 42 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 101 as allegedly including non-statutory subject matter in the claim term "computer-readable medium."

Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection, however, in order to expedite prosecution, Applicant has clarified the claim to recite statutory subject matter. Applicant respectfully submits that the scope of claim 42 is unchanged by this amendment.

Claims 1-8 and 10-42 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over U.S. Pub. No. 2015/0336271 to Spicer et al. ("Spicer") in view of U.S. Pub. No. 2017/0095930 to Warashina et al. ("Warashina").
Claim 9 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Spicer in view of Warashina, and further in view of U.S. Pub. No. 2018/0345483 to Sirkett et al. ("Sirkett").
Applicant respectfully traverses the rejections.
The Applicant respectfully asserts the applied references do not teach, suggest, disclose, or render obvious the presently-recited features of the claims.

Initially, Applicant respectfully submits that Spicer is silent regarding positioning the "second feature of a second subcomponent relative to the first calculated location of the first feature" (emphasis added). Thus, Spicer is silent with respect to the recited subject matter of claim 1. Spicer is completely silent regarding the positioning of the second feature based on the calculated location of the first feature. As admitted in the office action Spicer discloses "the relative position may include a predetermined standoff distance." Therefore based on the discloser in Spicer neither the first feature nor the second feature are determined by a calculated location of the other feature.

Applicant notes that the addition of Warashina fails to cure the above-noted defects of Spicer. Warashina merely discloses a generic second robot starting position that is in the vicinity of the target mark 6. See, e.g., Warashina at para. [0055]. Warashina then moves the second robot, not the first feature, to align the robot arm 23. Id. at para. [0037], [0056], and [0057]. Warashina does not disclose or suggest a second robot positioning a second feature of a second subcomponent relative to a first calculated location of a first feature. Thus, any modification of Spicer based on Warashina fails to disclose or suggest the subject matter of claim 1.

Moreover, any modification of Warashina to teach the recited subject matter would violate the principle of operation of Warashina. The technology disclosed in Warashina does not allow for the repositioning of two features relative to one another as recited in claim 1 and is therefore unable to be modified and/or combined with Spicer to arrive at the recited subject matter for at least the reasons discussed above.

The ancillary Sirkett reference fails to remedy the deficiencies of Spicer and Warashina. Thus, any modification of Spicer and/or Warashina based on Sirkett fails to disclose or suggest the subject matter of claim 1.
Therefore, based on the foregoing, no combination of the applied references can teach, suggest, disclose, or render obvious at least the feature of "receiving a second target location

indicating where a second robot is to position a second feature of a second subcomponent relative to the first calculated location of the first feature of the first subcomponent" as recited by independent claim 1. Thus, claim 1 is patentable over any combination of the recited references.

Independent claim 20, 40 and 41 disclose similar subject matter to independent claim 1 and are therefore allowable for at least the same reasons. The remaining claims depend from one of independent claims 1 or 20, and thus are patentable over the applied references for at least the same reasons, as well as being separately patentable based on the combination of subject matter recited therein.
Thus, Applicant respectfully requests the withdrawal of the rejection of the claims under 35 USC 103.

If for any reason the Examiner feels the application is not now in condition for allowance it is respectfully requested that they contact, by telephone, the undersigned practitioner at the indicated telephone number to arrange for an interview to expedite the disposition of this case.

Other than any fees submitted herewith, Applicant believes no further fees are owing. However, if a fee is due, please charge our Deposit Account Number 01-2300, under number 038191.00931 from which the undersigned is authorized to draw.
